newsitem.title: INDIA: India palm olein imports to rise ahead of festival.
newsitem.headline: India palm olein imports to rise ahead of festival.

text.p: India might import up to 250,000 tonnes of palm olein during the Hindu festival months of September and October to offset thin domestic supplies, industry officials said on Monday.

"There is an increased demand for edible oil during the festival months," said Dhanji Sawla, chairman of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT). "But the new domestic arrivals would start from late October.
"We therefore expect around 250,000 tonnes of palm olein imports from Malaysia during September and October," he said.
Analysts said demand for palm olein during the annual festival season between September and November was three times greater than during the rest of the year, and imports were bound to go up.
India's domestic stocks are the tightest between July and October.
Palm olein imports might touch nearly 300,000 tonnes during the months of September and October, said one analyst, who did not want to be identified.
India's edible oil imports in 1995/96 (November-October) are projected to touch 1.0 million tonnes compared to 700,000 tonnes in the previous year, according to industry officials.

Sawla said Malaysian palm olein export prices had risen nearly $28 in the past 10 days with China deciding to import palm oil. China last week approved imports of 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil between August 1996 and March 1997.
"But India would continue to buy even at this price as Indian oils are not available in bulk quantities ahead of the festival season," Sawla said.
Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange, said the domestic availability of edible oil was very poor. Therefore the total pressure was on palm olein.
India imported nearly 220,000 tonnes of palm olein between April and July, industry officials said.
